PullRequest.Title: chat: Share and rate-limit core utility model requests
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #340039

## What

VS Code core makes small "utility" model requests through the Copilot Language Model API wrapper: thinking-block titles, the goal summary, tool risk assessment, edit explanations, dictation cleanup and issue titles. Each feature sent its own requests with no shared limits. Restoring a long session sent one title request per thinking block, all at the same moment and again on every re-render. That produced the bursts of HTTP 429s in the issue, and titles that came back after a re-render were thrown away, so nothing got cached.

This PR:
- **Adds `IChatUtilityModelService`** (`contrib/chat/common`), which all six features now use to send their request. Each caller keeps its own model selection and error handling. The service:
  - Runs background requests (thinking titles) at most 3 at a time, with a 5 s timeout once each starts. Queued requests nobody is waiting for any more are dropped.
  - Lets requests with the same key share one pending request.
  - Holds back a model after a rate limit for the server's `retryAfter`, or 60 s if none, capped at 15 min.
  - Logs every request with the feature that made it, e.g. `[ChatUtilityModel] purpose=thinkingTitle background=true … outcome=success`.
- **Thinking titles:** a title that arrives after its block re-rendered is still stored and cached. While a title is queued, the block shows its fallback title after 2 s instead of a stale "Thinking".
- **Adds the `languageModelRateLimit` proposed API:** `LanguageModelError.RateLimited(message, retryAfter)`, with `retryAfter` in milliseconds like other API durations. The value now survives the trip across the extension-host boundary in both directions.
- **Copilot:** throws the new error with the server's `Retry-After` converted to milliseconds. It reports core requests to telemetry as `api.core/<purpose>` instead of `api.undefined`, using a private `_requestPurpose` model option that it only honours for requests from core.

## Why

Telemetry (`github.copilot-chat/response.error`, `type == rateLimited`, `source == api.undefined`) shows the share of active machines hitting these rate limits each day:

| Version | Share of active machines rate-limited per day |
|---|---|
| 1.138 / 1.139 | ~0.5% |
| 1.140 | ~2% |
| 1.141-insider | ~10% |

That came to about 14.5K machines on 2026-10-05. Core utility traffic accounts for about 70% of all rate-limited machines across every request source.

## Notes for reviewers

- **API review:** `vscode.proposed.languageModelRateLimit.d.ts` needs API review. The distro's `extensionEnabledApiProposals` entry for `GitHub.copilot-chat` needs `languageModelRateLimit` added.
- **Telemetry:** the `source` for core requests changes from `api.undefined` to `api.core/<purpose>`. Queries filtering on `api.undefined` need updating. The `api.` prefix is kept because Copilot uses it to exclude these requests from prompt-content telemetry.
- **Old error name:** Copilot's `ChatRateLimited` error is replaced by the new API error. `extHostChatAgents2` treats both as rate limits.
- **Interactive features during a rate limit:** goal summary, risk badges, explanations, dictation and issue titles now fail immediately through their existing error paths, instead of sending a request that would also get a 429.

## How to test

1. Open a long Agent Host session with many thinking or tool blocks and no cached titles. Reload the window, then switch between sessions.
2. Check the Window log for `[ChatUtilityModel]` lines. Background title requests should run at most 3 at a time, with no duplicate requests for the same block.
3. Check the GitHub Copilot Chat output channel for `[copilotLanguageModelWrapper/thinkingTitle]` request lines.
4. Reopen the session. Titles should come from the cache, with no new title requests.
5. While rate-limited, blocks show their fallback title and the log shows `outcome=skipped` until the `retryAfter` window passes.

## Validation

All commands were run on this branch, rebased onto `main`.

**Type-checks and lint**
- `npm run typecheck-client`: passed.
- In `extensions/copilot`: `npx tsc --noEmit --project tsconfig.json` and `npx tsc --noEmit --project tsconfig.worker.json`: passed.
- `npx eslint` on all changed core and Copilot files: passed.
- `node --experimental-strip-types build/hygiene.ts <changed files>`: passed. It also ran in the pre-commit hook.
- `npm run valid-layers-check`: passed.
- `npm run gulp compile-api-proposal-names`: the registry is up to date.

**Unit tests** (`./scripts/test.sh --runGlob …`)
- `**/contrib/chat/test/common/chatUtilityModelService.test.js`: passed (new).
- `**/chatContentParts/chatThinkingContentPart.test.js`: 142 passing.
- `**/contrib/chat/test/browser/chatSpeechToTextService.test.js`: 29 passing.
- `**/contrib/chat/test/browser/chatGoalSummaryService.test.js`: 4 passing.
- `**/contrib/chat/test/browser/tools/languageModelToolsService.test.js`: 144 passing.
- `**/api/test/browser/{extHostTypes,mainThreadLanguageModels}.test.js`: 49 passing.
- `**/api/test/common/extHost{LanguageModels,LanguageModelTools,ChatAgents2}.test.js`: 26 passing.
- `**/widget/chatListRenderer.test.js`: 731 passing, 6 failing. The 6 failures are `image tool icon alignment survives the reveal and restore (…)` and fail the same way on `main` without this change.

**Copilot specs** (`npx vitest --run`)
- `rateLimitBackoffMiddleware.spec.ts` and `copilotToken.spec.ts`: 53 passed.

**Not run:**
- Copilot extension-host tests.
- A manual run against a live rate-limited session.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The renderer-to-title-to-service call path, one key per block, and three-request drain limit are explicit in code, making the quadratic mechanism certain. Only the wall-clock magnitude varies with how many uncached blocks a user's long session contains.
Findings.PerformanceResource: UI-thread CPU spent scanning pending request objects and comparing keys
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For B uncached finalized thinking blocks, the three-wide limiter keeps nearly all B requests in `_pending`, so the per-request linear lookup performs about B(B-1)/2 key comparisons during cold restoration.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Quadratic CPU work can delay chat restoration and briefly block UI responsiveness in long sessions before the limited network work progresses.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Each thinking block sent directly through `ILanguageModelsService`; there was no shared pending collection and therefore no collection-wide scan for every title request.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every keyed utility request now linearly scans the full pending set before enqueueing. Restoring a long response finalizes one title per uncached thinking block, and line 1884 marks each as background so only three drain concurrently.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 71 introduces `Iterable.find(this._pending, ...)` on every keyed request; the same PR routes each thinking title through this keyed, three-wide background queue, so the growing scan did not exist before the diff.
Findings.Title: Index pending requests by key
Findings.Impact: Opening or rerendering a long chat with many uncached thinking blocks schedules one keyed title request per block; while model-selection continuations run on the workbench thread, lookup cost grows quadratically rather than linearly, causing avoidable restore latency/jank. Exact duration depends on session size, so severity is low, but the call path and scaling are deterministic.
Findings.Evidence: `chatListRenderer.finalizeThinkingPart` calls `finalizeTitleIfDefault` for completed thinking sections; `ChatThinkingContentPart` then calls `sendRequest` with a session/block cache key and `background: true`. The new limiter admits only three requests (line 82), leaving the rest in `_pending`, while line 71 scans that entire set for each subsequent block. The cache permits 1,000 stored entries and cold/missing entries all reach this path.
Findings.Recommendation: Maintain a `Map<string, IPendingRequest>` alongside the lifecycle set (insert in `_start`, delete in `_settle`) so keyed coalescing is O(1), while retaining the set only for unkeyed requests and disposal.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Each finalized uncached thinking block immediately started its own language-model request, so restoring a session with B blocks created B concurrent extension-host/network requests with no aggregate limiter or cross-render coalescing.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Long-session restoration could burst utility-model traffic and receive HTTP rate limits; the PR metadata reports 429 telemetry, while the changed call path and new concurrency test directly establish the prior unbounded fan-out.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: Thinking-title requests now enter one shared limiter capped at three active background requests, share an in-flight request by cache key, and drop queued requests after all callers cancel.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: The deleted base call at the blamed line directly invoked `sendChatRequest` from every block's title finalization. The added caller marks title requests `background: true` with a stable key, line 82 queues them in the service's three-wide limiter, and the added test asserts only three background requests run concurrently while duplicate `b1` callers produce one send.

Scenarios.Scenario: Cold or rerendered long chat session generates titles for finalized thinking blocks
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Rendering/finalizing each completed thinking section starts title generation asynchronously after model selection. Title text is not required for the chat row to render because a fallback appears after two seconds, but the keyed enqueue/lookup runs on the workbench event loop and can affect restoration responsiveness.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Language-model request crosses from workbench core to the extension-host model provider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One IPC request per distinct cold title key that starts; warm cache hits produce zero, duplicate pending keys share one, and rate-limited queued work is skipped before IPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same IPC request occurred once per rendered block, but all blocks started immediately and rerenders could duplicate it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the title fallback/render critical path after enqueue, but completion supplies and persists the generated title.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Copilot utility model HTTP request performed by the extension provider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One network call per distinct cold key that reaches the three-wide limiter; zero for warm cache hits, coalesced duplicates, canceled queued work, and requests skipped during backoff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One unbounded concurrent network request per uncached block, including duplicates after rerender; no aggregate limiter.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off initial row rendering because fallback text is available; completion updates/caches the title.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize the bounded profile title cache when each successful non-local title is persisted.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One serialization per successful caller continuation, over at most 1,000 entries; shared requests can have multiple continuations after rerenders.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Successful live parts already serialized the cache; the diff additionally allows a disposed owner to persist the shared result, trading bounded extra serialization for avoiding a later model request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs on title completion, not initial row rendering.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: B finalized thinking blocks without reusable generated/profile-cached titles. Each stable session/block key is distinct after in-flight deduplication, so effective cardinality is B; duplicate renders of the same key share one remote request.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Background model sends are globally limited to three. Requests beyond three remain pending; same-key callers share one promise. The added linear scan over this growing pending set makes cold enqueue CPU quadratic in B.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm profile-cache hits return before model selection and produce zero model calls. Cold misses enqueue one request per distinct key. Pending requests coalesce by key; canceled requests are dropped only before start. Failures are not negatively cached, while a model-level rate-limit entry suppresses sends until expiry.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: renderer finalization, unique cache keys, the three-wide limiter, and the full-set scan are explicit in code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The quadratic key-lookup mechanism is deterministic, but exact pause duration depends on the number of uncached blocks and hardware; this uncertainty is reflected in low severity.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable low-severity CPU regression: keyed coalescing linearly scans a pending set that grows with cold blocks, creating quadratic work during the exact long-session scenario the limiter targets. The remote boundary behavior itself is substantially improved.

Scenarios.Scenario: Advanced Autopilot goal summary for a submitted prompt
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The widget starts summarization without awaiting it before the main chat workflow; only the goal banner waits for the result, so the model call is off the chat request critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send one utility-model request through the language-model provider bridge.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One per unique cold prompt after LRU/in-flight grouping; zero on warm hits or active model backoff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The service directly made the same one IPC/model request per cold prompt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks only banner completion, not chat submission.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Copilot model request for the summary.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Same one per unique cold prompt; during known backoff the diff reduces this to zero.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same network call count absent shared rate-limit suppression.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One unique prompt per submitted request. Existing prompt-key LRU and in-flight maps reduce repeated identical prompts to zero warm calls or one shared cold call.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Interactive utility requests bypass the background limiter and start immediately. Multiple distinct widgets/prompts can overlap, unchanged from before; identical prompts are coalesced by the caller.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: LRU positive cache and per-prompt in-flight coalescing remain authoritative. Failures are not negatively cached. The new service adds model-level rate-limit backoff.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Prompt submission frequency and overlap vary, but the one-per-cold-key grouping is explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression: boundary cardinality is unchanged or reduced, and work stays off the main chat critical path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Tool risk assessment for confirmation badges or Advanced Autopilot gating
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Badge assessment is asynchronous and off initial rendering. In Advanced Autopilot, assessment is awaited before an otherwise auto-approved tool can execute, so one model request is on that tool invocation's critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send risk prompt through the language-model provider bridge.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One per distinct cold normalized tool key; zero for cached/in-flight duplicates and known model backoff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same direct IPC request was made per distinct cold assessment.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off badge rendering, but blocks Advanced Autopilot tool execution until assessment completes or fails.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Copilot utility model request for risk classification.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Same effective one per distinct cold key; known backoff suppresses calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same network operation with caller-side cache/coalescing but without shared rate-limit suppression.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Can add tool-start latency in the gated Autopilot path, unchanged except that known rate limits now fail immediately.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Distinct normalized tool-id/parameter/rubric keys. Existing result cache and in-flight map reduce duplicate keys to one call; multiple distinct tool calls can overlap.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Interactive assessments bypass the three-wide title limiter. Distinct assessments may overlap, as before; same-key requests coalesce in the risk service.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Caller-owned result cache and in-flight coalescing are unchanged. Model backoff is a shared timed negative state; failures otherwise are not negatively cached.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Concurrent distinct badge count depends on rendered tools, while gated tool calls are typically sequenced by agent execution.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression: the wrapper does not add boundary calls or serialization, and known rate limits shorten rather than extend the critical path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Generate explanations for chat edits across files
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A user/session explanation action groups all non-empty file diffs into one prompt and waits for one model response before explanation widgets complete.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send the grouped edit-diff prompt to the extension-host language-model provider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one for all non-empty diffs in an action, or zero when no model/backoff/cancellation applies.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Exactly one direct IPC/model request for the same grouped prompt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks explanation completion for the action.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Copilot utility-model request returning all explanations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One grouped network call per generation action; no per-file fan-out.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number and size of changed hunks across all files affect prompt/response size, but effective boundary cardinality remains one grouped request per generation action.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One grouped interactive request per action; it bypasses the background limiter. Separate actions could overlap, as before.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No response cache or request key is used. Cancellation propagates through the shared service; model rate-limit backoff can skip the request.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Prompt size varies with edit size, but this diff neither expands it nor changes request count.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression: the new service replaces local stream collection without changing grouping, bytes, concurrency, or critical-path boundary count.

Scenarios.Scenario: Optional language-model cleanup when dictation stops
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After transcription finalization, cleanup is awaited before the final transcript is returned. The existing outer timeout/cancellation bounds model selection and response consumption.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send bounded transcript and cleanup instructions through the language-model provider bridge.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one per eligible dictation stop; zero for disabled, empty, over-length, canceled, unavailable-model, or known-backoff cases.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same single IPC/model request was made and consumed under the same outer timeout.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: On final transcript latency, bounded by the caller's existing cleanup timeout.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Copilot utility-model request for punctuation/capitalization cleanup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one per eligible stop; known rate-limit backoff reduces it to zero.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same one network call and timeout path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: On dictation finalization; raw transcript remains fallback.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One bounded transcript per dictation stop; over-length transcripts are skipped before model selection, so effective model-call cardinality is at most one.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One cleanup per speech session; cancellation tears down replaced sessions. It is interactive and bypasses the title limiter, as the old direct request did.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No content cache or coalescing. A known model rate limit is a timed negative state and causes immediate raw-transcript fallback through existing error handling.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider response duration varies, but the existing timeout controls worst-case user latency.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression: request count, input bound, cancellation, and critical-path timeout remain equivalent; shared backoff can only avoid a doomed call.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: The user's generate-title action waits for extension registration, model selection, and one model response before filling or resetting the title UI; issue submission itself is separate.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send issue description through the extension-host language-model provider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One per successful explicit action, or zero with no model/known backoff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same single direct IPC/model request per action.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Copilot utility-model request for issue title.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One per explicit generation action; known backoff reduces calls.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One description per explicit click. No collection fan-out.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each click starts an interactive request immediately, matching prior behavior; there is no added limiter or serialization.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No title cache or in-flight key is used. Shared model backoff suppresses calls while rate limited.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: User click frequency is low and input length is user-controlled, unchanged by the diff.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression: wrapper substitution preserves one-request cardinality and response collection semantics.

Scenarios.Scenario: Language-model rate-limit error propagation and model-wide backoff
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A provider's rate-limit rejection crosses the extension-host/workbench RPC boundary with retry guidance. The first failing request pays the existing provider/network latency; subsequent utility requests for that model fail before IPC/network until expiry.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize/deserialize `LanguageModelError` and optional `retryAfter` across provider RPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One error payload for each request that actually reaches the provider and is rate-limited; skipped requests create no provider RPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Rate-limit errors already crossed RPC, but retry guidance was lost and core callers continued making requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Carries the rejection needed to stop subsequent work; serialization is constant-size.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Initial provider request receives an HTTP rate-limit response.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most the requests already in flight before the first error establishes backoff; later requests during the window make zero network calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Every feature invocation could send another network request despite an active server retry window.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The first error is on its feature path; later features fail immediately rather than wait for another 429.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of utility requests targeting the same model during the retry window. The backoff map has one entry per model identifier rather than per request.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The first concurrent failures can race before backoff is set; thereafter background queued tasks are skipped and interactive calls fail immediately. Title sends remain capped at three.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Timed negative state is keyed by model, defaults to 60 seconds, honors zero, and caps at 15 minutes. Entries remain in the map after expiry but model cardinality is small and lookups are O(1).
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: How many requests race before the first 429 depends on timing, but title concurrency is explicitly bounded to three.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression: constant-size error metadata adds negligible serialization and materially reduces repeated network work.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 26 changed files. Reported one low-severity repeated-work regression: keyed coalescing scans the growing pending set and becomes quadratic on cold long-session title restoration. Also recorded the PR's concrete fix for the prior unbounded thinking-title network burst. Other utility scenarios preserve or reduce effective IPC/network cardinality, retain caller cache/cancellation behavior, and add no reportable critical-path regression.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
